positive.prompt: Finance found a ledger discrepancy at month-end close that none of our monitoring caught
What should we alert on for our outbox and our nightly reconciliation job?
Every dashboard was green for three weeks while records were silently getting stuck
We have records sitting in PENDING forever and nothing fires because PENDING is a legal state

negative.prompt: Our p99 latency went from 200ms to 2s after the last deploy, help me find the regression
How do we stop a retry from charging the customer twice?
Should we fail open or fail closed when the rate limiter's Redis is unreachable?

evals.prompt: Read incident.md and monitoring.py. Answer the three questions the review left open.
evals.expected_output: Explains that every existing signal measures liveness and speed, that the reconciliation's silence is ambiguous, and that no run history exists to date the drift from.
expectations: States that worker_up, latency, throughput and error rate all stayed healthy because the process was healthy, and that none of them measures whether payouts are being completed
Identifies that reconcile_with_provider emits nothing on a clean run, so a job that found no discrepancies and a job that never ran produce identical silence
Identifies that the reconciliation queries only status = 'SENT', so the 311 stuck 'SENDING' rows were never examined — it reported clean on work it did not do
Says that no run history is recorded, so dating the drift required reconstruction, and proposes recording every run including clean ones

Proposes alarming on the age of the oldest unpublished outbox row rather than on outbox_depth, and explains that the flat depth after 13 Oct is indistinguishable from a healthy steady state by count alone
Does not propose fixing this by adding a threshold alert to payout_outbox_depth as the primary remedy

evals.prompt: Write the monitoring you would have wanted for this service.
evals.expected_output: Produces invariant queries, an age-based backlog alarm, a per-state gauge including SENDING, a job heartbeat, and a directional reconciliation result.
expectations: Writes at least one invariant as a query that runs outside the application, such as every SENT payout having a balanced ledger entry pair
Alarms on the age of the oldest unresolved item, not only on a count
Adds a gauge per payout state, including SENDING, and alarms on a record older than that state's allowed duration
Adds a heartbeat on successful completion of the nightly job and alarms on the absence of a recent one, outside the job itself
Reports reconciliation as matched, missing-locally and missing-remotely separately rather than as a single discrepancy count
Notes that running an invariant query in the test suite is nearly free once the query exists
